page: Amazon Web Services m7i.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the Geekbench single-core score reaching 2015.0 and single-threaded gzip compression processing at 33.37 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth read/write speeds fall into the lower performance tier. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in workloads like low-precision vector calculations and cryptography.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i.xlarge offers a modern DDR5 memory architecture and dedicated compute resources suitable for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. Given its strong single-threaded performance but weaker multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth, this instance is best suited for applications that prioritize single-core execution speed over massive parallelization. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, text processing, light database operations, and entry-level LLM inference for small models.
